workLog.task: Reproduce the defect and settle its mechanism
workLog.outcome: A four-line parent that prints then spawns with inherited descriptors emits CHILD before PARENT-BEFORE when stdout is piped or redirected to a file, and the expected order once sys.stdout.flush() is added. Byte counts are identical at 33 in both runs, so nothing is destroyed. Issue #3742 diagnosed this as the parent overwriting the child's bytes; that is wrong. Its reproduction ended in tail -4 and reordering had carried the gh error above that window.

Two conditional scans disagreed. One walked print() calls and missed output emitted through helpers such as _color_print. The other scoped to the enclosing function and missed a caller that printed before invoking the callee that spawns. Whether anything has reached stdout is not decidable at a call site, and flushing an empty buffer is free, so the rule applied is unconditional: flush before every fd-inheriting spawn. 24 sites across 20 files. scripts/ci/install_locked_deps.py already used print(..., flush=True) and was left alone.

workLog.task: Prove every inserted flush is load-bearing
workLog.outcome: Deleted each of the 24 inserted flushes one at a time and re-ran the detector. 24 caught, 0 missed. The guard's own negative control runs the piped parent both ways in-process and asserts the reordering, so the guard cannot outlive the defect.

stderr needs no flush: sys.stderr.line_buffering is True even when piped while sys.stdout.line_buffering is False. A test asserts that pair so the scope decision is checked rather than remembered. The deliberately vulnerable CWE-77 benchmark sample is allowlisted; editing it changes what the security detectors are measured against.
